He notes that the economy is already showing signs of contraction, with manufacturing, construction, mining, agriculture, transportation, and distribution already in recession. He also believes that the companies are ahead of the curve in terms of demoting employees, as they are reluctant to demote due to the tight labor market. Zandi concludes that the economy is on the brink of a strong slowdown, and the risks of a recession are high.

Title: Russia dodges technical recession in 2Q25

Summary: 
Russia’s Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat) released a preliminary estimate that GDP grew 1.1% year‑on‑year in the second quarter of 2025, giving a 1.2% y/y rise for the first half of the year. On a seasonally adjusted basis, GDP increased 0.4% quarter‑on‑quarter in 2Q25, rebounding from a 0.6% decline in 1Q25 and thereby avoiding a technical recession. Manufacturing contributed +3.8% y/y and the financial sector +11.0%, while wholesale and retail trade contracted –2% y/y. Analysts from Renaissance Capital warned that growth momentum may slow in the second half of 2025 and that full‑year GDP growth could fall below 1%, underperforming the Central Bank of Russia’s baseline scenario. The Central Bank’s own Research and Forecasting Department had previously estimated a 0.6% q/q contraction in 2Q25, and the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Economic Forecasting flagged the same recessionary sequence. At a September 12 press conference, CBR Governor Elvira Nabiullina said, 'According to our estimates, though these will be refined once detailed data are available, seasonally adjusted GDP in 2Q25 was higher than in 1Q25. Thus statements about a technical recession are, at this stage, highly debatable,' as cited by Kommersant. The Ministry of Economic Development still forecasts 2.5% GDP growth for 2025 but expects to revise this down to 1.2% in a mid‑September outlook. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov told President Putin that 2025 GDP growth could undershoot the official forecast of 2.5% and slow to 1.5%.

Published date: September 16 2025, 07:21

Title: US-Wirtschaft am Scheideweg: Droht eine Rezession oder folgt die Erholung?

Summary: 
The U.S. economy has entered a period of uncertainty. In August, the unemployment rate rose to 4.3 %, the highest level since 2021, while inflation remains below the historical average at 2.7 % (historical average 3.8 %). New data show that only 22,000 jobs were created and 13,000 were lost, resulting in the first net job loss since 2020 and the first time in four years that job seekers outnumbered vacancies. A New York Federal Reserve survey found that job‑seekers rate their prospects at 44.9 %, the lowest since the survey began in 2013, and many Americans expect rising unemployment and slower income growth. Consumers already feel higher living‑cost pressures; a survey projects a 3.2 % inflation rate for the next year, driven in part by persistent import tariffs that firms are passing on to consumers. "It is not hard to spot dark clouds on the horizon," said Alexander Field, a professor at Santa Clara University, adding that it is uncertain whether these clouds will bring a storm. Credit‑card debt has hit a record high, and the share of accounts with more than 90 days of delinquency is the highest in over a decade, indicating widespread difficulty keeping up with rising costs. While Field warns of a possible recession, Morgan Stanley analysts suggest the U.S. may be moving from a "rolling recession"—where only certain sectors slow—to a "rolling recovery," citing rising corporate profits and growing confidence among consumers and businesses. The Federal Reserve’s monetary policy will be pivotal; weak labor market data are increasing pressure to lower interest rates, which could further buoy the S&P 500, already at record highs this year.

Published date: September 09 2025, 13:33

URL: https://www.prosieben.de/serien/newstime/news/us-wirtschaft-am-scheideweg-droht-eine-rezession-oder-folgt-die-erholung-587320
